episodes.212755: During the 16th late afternoon and evening, a warm, humid airmass interacting with an approaching cold front and associated upper wave triggered scattered severe thunderstorms across central Indiana. Moderate instability and vertical wind shear promoted organized multicells and some supercells.||There were several severe hail reports, with diameters ranging from 1.00 and 1.25 inches impacting Carroll, Tippecanoe, Putnam, Hendricks, Marion, and Hancock counties. Straight-line thunderstorm wind gusts estimated between 58 mph and 60 mph also downed trees and large tree limbs across portions of Parke, Vigo, Putnam, and Morgan counties.||The primary severe event was a tornadic thunderstorm that tracked from Putnam County into western Morgan County. An EF-1 tornado touched down in Putnam County around 7:45 PM EST, with estimated maximum wind speeds of 105 mph. The tornado damaged several residences, destroyed an outbuilding, heavily impacted a mobile home, and snapped many trees. The tornado tracked along an 8.24-mile path across Putnam County before crossing into western Morgan County at 8:01 PM EST, weakening to an EF-0 with estimated peak winds of 70 mph. The tornado tracked an additional 1.13 miles causing minor tree damage before dissipating. The total path length was 9.37 miles. This severe weather event would be the fourth of many for the month which would eventually define a formal disaster period from June 6th to the 18th which was declared by the governor of Indiana.
episodes.213082: A wake low produced high winds during the late morning and early afternoon of June 17th. Wind gusts between 45 mph and 55 mph with a few higher gusts brought down numerous tree limbs. Scattered thunderstorms produced heavy rain and localized flash flooding during the mid afternoon across southeast Cook County. Isolated thunderstorms moved across far northern Illinois during the late evening of June 17th and produced one brief tornado.
episodes.213083: Scattered thunderstorms produced heavy rain and localized flash flooding across far northwest Indiana during the afternoon of June 17th.
episodes.213455: A supercell moving southeastward through southeast Kansas produced up to quarter size hail near Yates Center in Woodson County during the nighttime hours of June 16.
episodes.213506: A strong storm system for mid-June brought two rounds of thunderstorm on Wednesday June 17th. The strongest round of storms occurred during the morning hours that brough damaging winds (some significant), heavy rain, and two EF-1 tornadoes in Illinois which occurred in Monmouth and Warsaw. |Many trees fell and power lines were damaged, along with several reports of flash flooding. There were also 4-5 train cars that were pushed off the railroad just south of Monmouth, IL in Warren County due to significant straight-line winds (estimated near 100 mph). Additional train cars derailed as a result of these cars being blown off.

episodes.214102: Multiple rounds of flash flooding occurred throughout Southeast Texas over the course of several days, leading up to Tropical storm Arthur.
episodes.214348: Despite nebulous synoptic forcing and modest instability, several supercell thunderstorms developed ahead of a weak surface cold front across southwestern Kansas into far northwestern Oklahoma during the evening hours of the 16th. One such thunderstorm produced large to very large hail in Harper County, Oklahoma before dissipating.
episodes.214546: Several rounds of significant convection impacted central Illinois on June 17th, 2026.  Clusters of thunderstorms initially formed on the nose of a strong low-level jet streak across Iowa during the pre-dawn hours, then tracked southeastward along a warm frontal boundary into central Illinois through midday. Scattered damaging wind gusts were reported in north-central Illinois, with the most concentrated corridor of 60-70 mph winds focused along a Galesburg, to Peoria, to Chenoa line.||Thunderstorms re-developed along a remnant outflow boundary from the morning convection by mid to late afternoon, with the most intense cells materializing along and south of a Springfield to Paris line where several tornadoes occurred and hail larger than baseballs (3 diameter) was reported across portions of Moultrie, Douglas, and Coles counties. An EF2 tornado impacted the Mattoon to Charleston area, and an EF3 tracked just north of Effingham.
episodes.214612: Low level shear ahead of a cold front led to a couple of brief tornadoes across southeast Alabama that were captured on video. Damage was minimal.
episodes.214696: Strong warm advection ahead of an approaching northwest flow wave spawned several elevated thunderstorms, some of which organized into short bowing segments with 60 to 70 knots of effective shear and around 2000 J/kg MUCAPE. Convective wind gusts from 58 to 68 mph occurred near the Storm Lake area.
episodes.214704: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed along weak convergence in deep cyclonic flow, and despite weak MLCAPE up to 250-500 J/kg, very strong 850-700 hPa winds led to strong outflows on decaying storms with gusts locally 60 to 70 mph.
episodes.214705: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed along weak convergence in deep cyclonic flow, and despite weak MLCAPE up to 250-500 J/kg, very strong 850-700 hPa winds led to strong outflows on decaying storms with gusts locally 60 to 70 mph.
episodes.214706: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed along weak convergence in deep cyclonic flow, and despite weak MLCAPE up to 250-500 J/kg, very strong 850-700 hPa winds led to strong outflows on decaying storms with gusts locally 60 to 70 mph.
episodes.214781: Showers and thunderstorms developed across northern Maine during the afternoon of the 17th with diurnal instability. A strong thunderstorm in Saint Agatha produced 0.75 diameter hail.
episodes.215056: A cluster of thunderstorms developed within the vicinity of a strong mid-upper level shortwave trough and a surface low. One supercell tracked from southeast Minnesota through northeast Iowa and into southwest Wisconsin while maintaining is strength during the late afternoon. The storm evolved into a line as it trtacked through south central Wisconsin during the early evening and produced a swath of damaging winds and three tornadoes.
episodes.215115: A wake low produced high winds across parts of southern Lake Michigan during the late morning and early afternoon of June 17th. The Harrison Dever crib measured a peak wind gust to 58 knots.
episodes.215603: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved northward through Southeastern Arizona the afternoon and evening of June 17th, 2026. These storms caused thunderstorm wind damage causing 8 power poles to be downed and 7,000 customers to be without power in the Tucson Metro and damage to a power transformer that caused a power outage for Tohono O'odham Nation. Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms caused flash flooding in normally dry rivers and washes that resulted in multiple swift water rescues that resulted in 1 fatality and 2 injuries. Additionally, multiple roadways in Cochise County was impassible due to flooding. An estimated penny sized hail was reported on the SW side of Tucson.
episodes.215604: This long-track EF-2 tornado developed about 5 miles east of Waukon during the late afternoon hours and trekked east-southeast through Allamakee County resulting in significant tree damage and some structural damage. The tornado eventually reached the Mississippi River just north of Harpers Ferry, where it crossed into Crawford County, Wisconsin near US Lock and Dam No. 9.
episodes.215669: During the late afternoon and early evening hours on June 17th, two long-tracked tornadoes moved across portions of Crawford and Grant Counties. The first of these tornadoes was an EF-2 which moved into Crawford County from northeast Iowa and resulted in several instances of tree and structural damage before dissipating near Boscobel. The second tornado, which was rated EF-1, formed just southeast of Boscobel and moved east-southeast through Grant County resulting in various instances of tree and structural damage before exiting into Iowa County.
episodes.215717: An upper level trough was moving southeast through southern New Mexico with some mid level moisture available for thunderstorms to develop.  A very dry surface with dew point depressions over 65 degrees allowed for gusty thunderstorm winds to occur.  Blowing dust also developed over the Lordsburg Playa causing the interstate to be closed for a short period.
episodes.215843: A storm moving offshore from Melbourne produced severe wind gusts.
episodes.215844: A thunderstorm moving offshore produced a severe wind gust in Melbourne.
episodes.215875: Broad cyclonic flow and subtle shortwave energy aloft along with a weak surface boundary and ample moisture in the vicinity led to an environment capable for a strong thunderstorm across local waters.
episodes.215995: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms moved over Lake Erie in the evening hours.
